prerequisites: It is recommended that the student has previously taken the Basic Communication Services course.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to write, develop and sign projects in the field of telecommunication engineering aimed at the conception and development or exploitation of telecommunication and electronics networks, services and applications.
Knowledge of basic subjects and technologies, which enables learning new methods and technologies, and provides great versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities, understanding the ethical and professional responsibility of the Telecommunication Technical Engineer's activity.
Facility for handling specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.

Ability to work in a multidisciplinary team and in a multilingual environment, and to communicate, both in writing and orally, knowledge, procedures, results and ideas related to telecommunications and electronics.
Ability to autonomously learn new knowledge and techniques suitable for the conception, development or exploitation of telecommunication systems and services.

Ability to conceive, deploy, organize and manage telecommunication networks, systems, services and infrastructures in residential (home, city and digital communities), business or institutional contexts, taking responsibility for their implementation and continuous improvement, as well as knowing their economic and social impact.
Knowledge and use of the fundamentals of programming in telecommunication networks, systems and services.
Knowledge and use of network architecture concepts, protocols and communication interfaces.

Ability to differentiate the concepts of access and transport networks, circuit and packet switching networks, fixed and mobile networks, as well as distributed network systems and applications, voice, data, audio, video and interactive and multimedia services.
Knowledge of telecommunication regulations at national, European and international levels.

Ability to apply the techniques on which telematic networks, services and applications are based, such as management, signaling and switching systems, routing, security (cryptographic protocols, tunneling, firewalls, billing mechanisms, authentication and content protection), traffic engineering (graph theory, queuing theory and teletraffic) pricing and reliability and quality of service, in fixed, mobile, personal, local or long-distance environments, with different bandwidths, including telephony and data. (Only acquired in the Telematics specialization)
Ability to design telematic network and service architectures.
Ability to program telematic, networked and distributed services and applications.

Evaluate possible technological solutions to provide a given service, based on initial conditions and the search for applicable regulations, recommendations, etc., and select the most appropriate one based on technical, economic and/or other criteria.
Properly present and document the resolution of a problem, work, or project related to telecommunication systems.
Work in a team to design and evaluate the performance of multimedia and interactive services.
Take initiative to propose and evaluate alternative or novel solutions to problems arising from the design, configuration and implementation of voice, data, multimedia and interactive services.
Effectively communicate (in expression and comprehension), orally and in writing, the characteristics of the designed communication services.

syllabus_topics: Transport protocols and description of multimedia sessions
Scalability and evaluation of media distribution services
VoIP services in a domestic environment
RTC services in a corporate environment
Audio and video capture and storage
Audio and video encoding and playback
Development of a multimedia and interactive service using Git and deployment on a cloud server.

assessment_methods.method: Theory (two partial controls or final global exam)
Laboratory practices (two partial controls or final global exam)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade is calculated as 0.3 * Theory + 0.1 * Classroom Practices + 0.3 * Lab Practices + 0.3 * Teamwork. A minimum of 5 points in Theory, 3 in Lab Practices, and 5 in Teamwork (out of 10) is required to pass; otherwise, the final grade is the minimum of the formula result and 4.5. Lab Practices require 80% attendance, and Teamwork requires active participation in the public defense. For extraordinary calls, theory and lab practices can be re-evaluated via a global exam, while classroom practices and teamwork grades are carried over; the same passing criteria apply. For differentiated evaluation, the final grade is 0.3 * Theory + 0.3 * Practices + 0.4 * Individual Work, requiring at least 5 points in each part, otherwise the final grade is the minimum of the formula result and 4.5.
